claims.text: Adding approximately 1 wt% Zr to the baseline refractory high-entropy alloy will produce coherent nanoscale Zr-rich precipitates.
The baseline refractory high-entropy alloy lacks controlled nanoscale precipitates.
The Zr-rich precipitates will be distributed throughout the alloy microstructure.
Coherent nanoscale Zr-rich precipitates will hinder dislocation motion at elevated temperatures.
Hindering elevated-temperature dislocation motion through precipitate strengthening will increase high-temperature yield strength.
The low Zr addition level will preserve room-temperature mechanical performance.
Adding approximately 1 wt% Zr will leave the alloy density nearly unchanged.
At 800–900 °C under tensile loading, the Zr-modified alloy will exhibit approximately 10–20% greater yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The Zr-modified alloy will maintain room-temperature ductility comparable to that of the baseline alloy.
The Zr-modified alloy will have density comparable to that of the baseline alloy.
The predicted benefit depends on forming a uniform dispersion of nanoscale precipitates.
Excessive Zr segregation or coarse precipitate formation may eliminate the high-temperature strengthening benefit.
Excessive Zr segregation or coarse precipitate formation may degrade room-temperature performance.
The magnitude of high-temperature strengthening and the critical precipitate morphology depend on processing conditions.
